title: The Emperor's True Portrait (MR)
summary: Akbar is blind in one eye and walks with a limp. Three painters attempt his portrait. Birbal shows how true genius captures reality with grace. [MR]
full_text:
Emperor Akbar, though majestic and powerful, had two physical flaws from old battle injuries: his left eye was partially blind and clouded, and his right leg had a slight limp from a war arrow.

Akbar summoned three famous portrait artists from Delhi, Lahore, and Kashmir to paint his imperial likeness, promising ten thousand gold coins for a portrait that was both completely truthful and completely royal.

The first artist painted Akbar with both eyes wide, bright, and perfect, and both legs straight as pillars.

Akbar frowned: 'Flattery! You have painted an imaginary king, not me! You lie to please my vanity!' The first painter was dismissed without reward.

The second artist, determined to be fiercely realistic, painted Akbar with a milky, twisted, blind eye and a shriveled, deformed leg.

Akbar was offended: 'Insolence! You have focused on my infirmity, turning the Emperor of Hindustan into a wretched cripple, ignoring the majesty of the throne!' The second painter was dismissed.

The third artist, young and nervous, consulted Birbal before lifting his brush. Birbal whispered: 'Art must marry truth with dignity. Paint what the Emperor does, not merely what he suffers.'

Two weeks later, the third artist unveiled his masterpiece before the imperial durbar.

The portrait depicted Emperor Akbar mounted upon a noble Arabian stallion during a hunt.

Akbar was drawn in profile, drawing a great golden bow to shoot an arrow at a charging wild boar!

Because he was aiming his bow, his wounded left eye was naturally closed in marksman focus, while his good right eye aimed straight along the arrow!

And because he was mounted upon his horse, his legs were tucked into the stirrups under his saddle blankets, concealing the slight limp while displaying supreme equestrian grace!

The portrait was completely, undeniably true to life, yet captured the Emperor at the absolute peak of martial majesty, strength, and royal honor!

Akbar leaped from his throne with tears of admiration: 'Magnificent! You have hidden nothing, lied about nothing, and yet honored the throne with supreme dignity!'

Akbar awarded the young artist twenty thousand gold mohurs, while Birbal smiled, remarking that wisdom finds the angle where truth and beauty become one.
